entries.title: Katamari Damacy
entries.subtitle: The room changes when you grow
entries.summary: Katamari Damacy makes growth change the meaning of an ordinary room: what blocks the ball now may become part of it later.
body: Namco released Katamari Damacy for PlayStation 2 in Japan on 18 March 2004. A small Prince must rebuild the stars by rolling a sticky ball through everyday surroundings. Two analogue sticks control its movement, and objects collected along the route become part of the growing mass.

Size changes the job of the scenery. An object too large to collect can first act as an obstacle, then become useful material once the ball grows. The player revisits the same surroundings with different possibilities, so progress changes how the room is read rather than simply opening another door.

The peculiar royal story and varied vocal music give that repeated action a playful tone. Namco's contemporary announcement presented simple operation alongside strong musical character. The 2018 REROLL edition later renewed the graphics; the accompanying high-definition image shows that recreation, not a falsely enlarged capture from the original PlayStation 2 release.
story_headings: A world with its own musical voice

entries.title: Lumines
entries.subtitle: A line turns a pattern into a beat
entries.summary: Lumines lets a moving musical line decide when a finished visual pattern becomes a cleared space.
body: Lumines began on PSP in Japan on 12 December 2004, with North American and European releases following in 2005. Q Entertainment's puzzle used a portable screen and headphones as parts of one experience. Its coloured blocks, changing visual skins and music were designed to be encountered together.

Falling two-by-two pieces contain two colours. Arranging their cells into larger matching squares prepares a group for removal, but a line moving with the music decides when that removal happens. Making a combination and waiting for it to clear are therefore separate parts of the same decision.

Tetsuya Mizuguchi later described the original idea as a way to combine strong visuals, music and interaction on a machine carried like a personal music player. Actions add sounds aligned to the beat. The 2018 Remastered image accompanying this story shows the shared core clearly, while its modern presentation is distinguished from the original PSP release.
